findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Mark each Testing bullet as delivered-here (DET-tier: presence/shape, syntax, grandfathering) vs. deferred-to-98df (live AGENT contradiction/privilege/no-anchor/calibration), so the Testing section and the Descoped section agree.
evidence: Testing: 'Contradiction detection, contract tier: ... This is the regression test for the actual escape — build the fixture from the real one'
Testing: 'Privilege-posture case', 'No-anchor fallback case (T8)', 'Calibration: corpus replay per ADR-0054'

Descoped: 'that rule (a) fires on an environment contradiction, (b) stays silent with no in-repo anchor, (c) flags privilege_posture: broader ... They are NOT delivered here and are NOT claimed as done. They moved to 98df because proving them requires an eval corpus ... plus a live semantic run'
No AC in this story covers the contradiction/privilege/no-anchor/calibration tests — they map to descoped runtime behaviour, yet Testing presents them as this story's regression tests.
findings.finding: The Testing section lists tests (contradiction detection, privilege-posture case, no-anchor fallback, corpus-replay calibration) that require the live AGENT criterion to run, but the Descoped section moves exactly those runtime-behaviour proofs to sibling 98df and states they are NOT delivered or claimed here. The two sections send an implementer in opposite directions on whether these tests are built in this story.
scenarios: An implementer reads Testing and tries to build the contradiction-detection regression test, then discovers it needs the descoped live AGENT run and eval corpus.
A reviewer cannot tell which Testing bullets are in-scope deliverables versus 98df's.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the Testing section into 'Delivered here (DET, no LLM)' — presence/shape unit test, declaration-syntax test, grandfathering advisory test — and 'Deferred to 98df (requires eval corpus + live run)' — contradiction detection, privilege-posture, no-anchor fallback, calibration; matching the Descoped section.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the Testing section with the 98df descope: mark the contradiction / privilege-posture / no-anchor tests as DEFERRED-to-98df (they need the eval corpus + live semantic run) and keep only the DET-check unit tests, the syntax-binding test, the grandfathering advisory test, and the prompt-loadability test as THIS story's deliverable coverage.
evidence: Testing: 'Contradiction detection, contract tier: a plan declaring account X against a repo whose Terraform backend names account Y produces a finding. This is the regression test for the actual escape'

Descoped section: 'that rule (a) fires on an environment contradiction, (b) stays silent with no in-repo anchor, (c) flags privilege_posture: broader... They are NOT delivered here and are NOT claimed as done... proving them requires an eval corpus... plus a live semantic run'
No delivered AC asserts the AGENT criterion fires; ACs cover only DET presence/shape, overlay structure, prompt existence/loadability, contract-untouched
findings.finding: The Testing section lists contract-tier tests that require the AGENT criterion to run semantically — 'Contradiction detection', 'Privilege-posture case', and 'No-anchor fallback case (T8)' — but the 'Descoped to 98df' section explicitly moves exactly those runtime behaviours to the child ticket and states they 'are NOT delivered here and are NOT claimed as done' because they 'require an eval corpus plus a live semantic run'. The Testing section thus promises coverage this story cannot deliver, and none of the delivered ACs assert the AGENT criterion actually fires on a contradiction. An implementer reading Testing could believe those tests are in-scope here.
findings.location: Testing section (bullets: 'Contradiction detection, contract tier', 'Privilege-posture case', 'No-anchor fallback case (T8)') vs 'Descoped to 98df' section
findings.suggested_fix: In the Testing section, split the bullets into 'Delivered here (DET + wiring)' and 'Deferred to 98df (AGENT runtime behaviour, requires eval corpus + live run)', matching the Descoped section so the two sections cannot be read as contradictory.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add one paragraph noting the SLSA / in-toto provenance-attestation prior art (the where/when/how/under-what model) and stating why a bespoke repo-local four-field text declaration is chosen over aligning with that established vocabulary.
evidence: SLSA provenance spec (slsa.dev/spec/.../provenance): provenance is 'verifiable information about software artifacts describing where, when and how something was produced'
in-toto/SLSA attestation model pairs a claim with the environment and identity that produced it — directly analogous to the proposed fields
Plan grounds itself entirely in internal precedents; no external provenance-framework is named
findings.finding: The plan crosses the security/auth and external-integration bright-lines and introduces a four-field measurement-provenance schema (environment/principal/privilege_posture/instrument), but considers only INTERNAL prior art (ADR-0043/0054, det_operator_attested, T5c, E4). It does not consider the closely-matching external prior art in software-supply-chain provenance attestation (SLSA / in-toto), whose canonical model is 'verifiable information describing WHERE, WHEN, HOW and under WHAT a thing was produced' — essentially the same predicate the plan proposes for measurements.
findings.location: Approach §1 / Scope; the four-field provenance schema
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer asks why rebar invents a bespoke provenance schema instead of aligning field names/semantics with an established attestation vocabulary
The schema later needs to interoperate with or emit standard attestations and finds its ad-hoc field set diverges from SLSA/in-toto predicates
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach §1 or the Context section, briefly acknowledge SLSA/in-toto provenance attestations as the established prior art for capturing measurement/build context, and justify the lightweight repo-local declaration (parsed by a DET check, refutable against in-repo IaC) as the right-sized lever for a ticket-level gate rather than a full attestation framework.
